method: Both original samples received atomscan and cleave facts; decoded text and PE/CLR metadata were inspected. dnfile/dncil resolved every managed method body, entry points, call targets and string operands. No sample was executed locally.

evidence: Exact byte comparison against filF23135311FD413DA3A6A8DD4B38FBBC4 in the independently downloaded same-version release MSI succeeded.

Entry 0x060003eb / RVA 0x1843c, Program.Main: dispatches RunFile, RunFileElevated, StartService, Rerun and RunRole. Default startup parses argv or ClickOnce ActivationUri using ClientLaunchParameters.FromUrl/FromQueryString; throws if parameters cannot be supplied. Creates SocketEndPointManager and Client, then Application.Run. A getter for ClientLaunchParametersConstraint is not an embedded constraint value.

Client.ProcessMessage (0x06000109 / RVA 0x72bc) dispatches input, clipboard, virtual-file, credentials, printing, command and configuration messages. Transferred-file handler 0x060007fc copies virtual files, then optionally calls RunFileAsync with requested elevation. This is ordinary powerful remote-support functionality, with no supplied unauthorized tasking.

Program.RunFileAsync (0x060003ec / RVA 0x187ac) passes its own executable path to TryUnblockFile before relaunching itself with RunFile/RunFileElevated and the requested file. The release ScreenConnect.Windows helper at 0x06000102 / RVA 0x72bd appends :Zone.Identifier and calls DeleteFile. The new trait reports the helper reference, not observed deletion or an evasion objective.

StartService launches ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe, or a credentialed WindowsClient StartService child, and waits for the result. runas requests normal elevation. ACL preparation grants Everyone ReadAndExecute (131241), with no arbitrary-write grant or observed UAC bypass.

ExtractManifestAttachmentsIfFirstRun at 0x06000660 / RVA 0x22ec8 reads external deployment-manifest XML comments in filename/base64 pairs and writes attachments with CreateNew. No deployment manifest or decoded attachment payload is in this sample. Debugger.IsAttached opens a TraceForm rather than avoiding execution.

Screen capture, audio, clipboard, credential-entry dialogs, file transfer and remote printing fit the advertised client. No fixed relay, session token, instance key, packed executable stage, credential-store harvester or unrelated payload was found in these bytes.
Exact byte comparison against filC1D18007D3175279B0EDD654D18B0CA5 in the independently downloaded same-version release MSI succeeded.

Entry 0x06000006 / RVA 0x20a0 initializes logging, DLL hardening and WinForms. Creates IFileOpenDialog, obtains ProfilesDirectory through the registry, sets the initial folder and displays ScreenConnect File Manager.

SetWindowsHookEx installs WH_GETMESSAGE (3) and WH_CALLWNDPROCRET (12) hooks for GetCurrentThreadId; SetWinEventHook is scoped to that thread. Traced callbacks reroute mouse-wheel messages, customize menus/drawing and adjust dialog/tree controls. They do not implement keyboard logging or remote-process injection.

OnFileOk callback 0x06000010 / RVA 0x229e obtains the selected shell path and calls Process.Start(new ProcessStartInfo(path) { UseShellExecute = true }). No fixed command, downloader, outbound channel, persistence installer or credential theft occurs in this GUI helper.

packaging_and_trust: Both are IL-only strong-name-marked PEs with reproducible-build markers, coherent version/product fields and no managed ManifestResource payloads. Future-looking COFF/debug timestamps are factual build metadata, not demonstrated timestomping.

Authenticode digests match and RSA signer/timestamp verification succeeds with revocation checking disabled. Normal osslsigncode verification fails because the shared Connectwise, LLC certificate is revoked. Certificate thumbprint 82b4e7924d5bed84fb16ddf8391936eb301479cec707dc14e23bc22b8cdeae28; serial 0B9360051BCCF66642998998D5BA97CE. Signing times: 2025-04-08 18:36:29 UTC (client), 18:35:30 UTC (file manager). Retain the suspicious compromised-certificate trait on both.

Certificate tables end at EOF. ASN.1 inspection shows only the Microsoft RFC3161 timestamp unsigned attribute (1.3.6.1.4.1.311.3.3.1), with respectively 3 and 4 bytes of zero alignment padding; no appended launch settings or payload.

The vendor describes certificate revocation and subsequent changes that separate customization data from signed binaries. This explains product trust history; it does not establish authorization of a deployment.

trace: Core FixupAppDomain returns immediately. Windows FixupProcess limits DLL search to System32 and sets image-load mitigation; exception hooks register ordinary logging handlers.

Client SocketEndPointManager.RunThread constructs relay:// from supplied Host and Port, connects through ClientToolkit.ConnectNetworkConnection, retries with backoff, generates secret/random bytes and encrypts the secret with the supplied RSA key before establishing its channel. No fixed attacker endpoint is in this traced path.

Windows StartProcessInSameDirectory uses Process.Start and optional runas; TryUnblockFile deletes the supplied path alternate stream. Actual adjacent dependency copies from the original deployment were not supplied.
Other complete embedded URLs belong to DigiCert certificate/OCSP/CRL records. The client literal http:// is a prefix prepended to a user-supplied proxy address, not an embedded endpoint.

findings: Retrieved the actual HTML reports via curl after the browsing tool could not access them. Both static reports score 8 and name Revoked Certificate in Chain, Signed with revoked ConnectWise certificate and Untrusted Codesign Signers. Behavioral1 scores 3 for each and reports Requests/TCP/UDP all zero.

Behavioral process trees show each bare component launched without session parameters, followed by the .NET dw20.exe crash reporter. Most processor/BIOS and privilege indicators are attributed to dw20.exe. WriteProcessMemory indicator target PIDs match dw20.exe children; the client report has inconsistent target procid numbering. This is consistent with crash-reporting interaction, not proof of an injected implant. Neither sample nor the inspected release dependencies references WriteProcessMemory/CreateRemoteThread/VirtualAllocEx in managed code.

verdict_balance: BENIGN describes these isolated release-identical components, whose traced behavior matches remote support/file browsing. The signed-release identity plus execution-path analysis outweigh generic PUA/RemoteAdmin/HackTool labels and revoked signing as evidence of malicious modification. Their collection is explained by abuse-relevant remote-administration capabilities and revoked signing, explicitly responsible for the sandbox static score. No original wrapper, deployed configuration/DLL set, endpoint execution history or operator authorization was provided. Abuse remains possible; queue routing to sighted quarantine remains appropriate.

trait_changes.reason: Names the observed setting/getter reference, not an MSI-only configured value. Whole-word matching rejects longer identifiers; all four local consumers were updated. Identity remains in the existing ScreenConnect leaf; no relocation or product exception was introduced.

Notable neutral file-deletion helper reference, following fs/delete/file library API observation placement. Reference alone establishes no execution or unauthorized cleanup. Existing directory/ancestor consumers were audited and final sample scans show no unsupported escalation.
